question.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}\frac{8-4\sqrt{x}}{x-4} & =\frac{8-4\sqrt{4}}{4-4}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we need to first simplify the limit. Since the radical is in the numerator, we can multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the numerator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}\frac{8-4\sqrt{x}}{x-4} & ={lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}\frac{4(2-\sqrt{x})}{x-4} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}\frac{4(2-\sqrt{x})(2+\sqrt{x})}{(x-4)(2+\sqrt{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}\frac{4({2}^{2}-{(\sqrt{x})}^{2})}{(x-4)(2+\sqrt{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}\frac{4(4-x)}{(x-4)(2+\sqrt{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}\frac{-4(x-4)}{(x-4)(2+\sqrt{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}\frac{-4}{2+\sqrt{x}} \\  & =\frac{-4}{2+\sqrt{4}} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
